A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diencephalic cell loss in the infant and adult hemidecorticates is similar in many respects, but that there are some differences in degree of cell loss.
the thalamic nuclei of newborn monkeys are more susceptible to retrograde cell degenerative effects of cortical lesions than the nuclei of adult monkeys.

the newborn monkeys had more severe retrograde cell degenerations than did the adults in the following thalanic nuclei: anterior medialis, pars lateralis; ventrobasalis; ventral lateralis; pulvinaris and geniculatus; and in the following extrathalamic areas: medial mamillary nucleus and nucleus of the diagonal bands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thalamus of the infant macaque is more vulnerable to retrograde cell degenerative changes than that of the adult monkey.
there are significant differences between the newborn and young adult monkeys in the extent of retrograde cell degenerations following hemidecortication.
the newborn monkey has an extensive diencephalic projection from the cerebral cortex, whereas in the adult monkey the projection has been reduced to a few thalamic nuclei.
